written_by: hand, copied from the cited paper; not generated by tools/other-half-data.mjs
what: Logical errors per round on Google's 105-qubit chip of 2024, each recording read afterwards by two decoders. These are Google's measurements, quoted. None of it is the group's own.

status.distance_7_and_lambda: from the main text of the paper (Sec. II), checked against the paper on 15 November 2026
status.distance_3_and_5: from Table S1 of the supplement; confirmed against the arXiv PDF in the fact check of 16 November 2026

decoders.label: neural network
decoders.paper_name: neural network decoder, fine-tuned on data from the chip

note_qubits: Qubit counts are the code's own (2d² − 1). The chip uses 101 at distance 7: 49 storing, 48 helpers and 4 more for removing leakage.
note_recordings: The values at distances 3 and 5 are averages over 9 and 4 sub-grids of the chip. Each distance is therefore its own recording; within a distance both decoders read the same data.
